nodes.label: Reason Engine
nodes.rationale: Verifies each rule against evidence found in the email before showing a plain-language reason to ensure the system never makes unsupported claims.

nodes.label: Sender Profiles Table
nodes.rationale: Updated only from known-good uploads or LOW-risk analyses to prevent history poisoning from compromised or spoofed senders.

nodes.label: Evidence Verification Rule System
nodes.rationale: Templates filled with real extracted values; discarding rules when evidence is missing avoids hallucination and unsubstantiated claims.

nodes.label: 57 Features in Six Groups
nodes.rationale: Numeric features are scaled to 0-1 so linear models and SHAP behave well; unavailable evidence gets explicit missing flags.

nodes.label: Feature Extraction Engine
nodes.rationale: Exact same feature extraction code runs at training and inference time to eliminate train/serve parity skew.

nodes.label: Risk Scorer
nodes.rationale: Uses thresholds pulled from versioned config to allow past results to remain explainable when retuned.

nodes.label: SHAP Explainer Engine
nodes.rationale: TreeExplainer is exact and fast enough for synchronous per-request evaluation; reference background sample kept in memory.

nodes.label: Sender History Store
nodes.rationale: Below message-count threshold, behavioral features set an insufficient_history flag to prevent false confidence.

nodes.label: PhishLens System Architecture (v1 Design)
nodes.rationale: Built as a modular monolith to be shippable solo, with clean seams so any piece can be pulled into its own service later without a rewrite.

nodes.label: Modular Monolith Architecture
nodes.rationale: One deployable FastAPI service whose internal modules have clear boundaries, plus Supabase and React, allowing any module to be separated later without rewriting others.

nodes.label: ADR-001: Modular Monolith
nodes.rationale: Small team needs something runnable, debuggable and deployable quickly; microservices avoided in v1 while maintaining clean module boundaries.

nodes.label: ADR-002: Inbound Email Webhook First
nodes.rationale: Webhook provider requires minimal setup compared to Gmail API OAuth consent, Pub/Sub, and token refresh.

nodes.label: ADR-003: Shared Feature Code for Training and Serving
nodes.norm_label: adr-003: shared feature code for training and serving
nodes.rationale: Prevents train/serve skew by using backend/app/features/ in both training and inference; registry enforces exact feature name and ordering match.

nodes.label: ADR-004: Synchronous Processing First
nodes.rationale: Typical pipeline latency is low; avoids operational overhead of message queues until p95 latency under load demands an asynchronous queue.

nodes.label: ADR-005: Template-based explanations, no LLM in v1
nodes.norm_label: adr-005: template-based explanations, no llm in v1
nodes.rationale: Explanations must be faithful and cheap; literature warns LLM text can hallucinate features (Cau et al. 2025). Traceable sentences with zero API cost.

nodes.label: ADR-006: Forwarding: prefer attachment; treat inline authentication as missing
nodes.norm_label: adr-006: forwarding: prefer attachment; treat inline authentication as missing
nodes.rationale: Inline forwards are re-sent by the forwarder, causing original SPF/DKIM/DMARC results to be lost. Treating inline authentication as missing avoids false 'failed authentication' alarms.

nodes.label: ADR-007: Sender history only from safe or known-good mail
nodes.norm_label: adr-007: sender history only from safe or known-good mail
nodes.rationale: Prevent adversarial poisoning where an attacker repeatedly sends spoofed mail to make a sender appear normal.

nodes.label: ADR-008: Evidence-verified reasons and a generic fallback
nodes.norm_label: adr-008: evidence-verified reasons and a generic fallback
nodes.rationale: Model attribution can point to features whose evidence is absent or misleading; checking reasons against extracted evidence prevents hallucinated statements.

nodes.label: ADR-009: Synthetic generator is for pipeline testing only
nodes.norm_label: adr-009: synthetic generator is for pipeline testing only
nodes.rationale: Real corpora take time to collect and pipeline testability is required immediately, but generator artifacts/leaks (e.g. history cues) mean numbers should never be reported as results.

nodes.label: ADR-010: SQLAlchemy with SQLite for development and PostgreSQL (Supabase) for production
nodes.norm_label: adr-010: sqlalchemy with sqlite for development and postgresql (supabase) for production
nodes.rationale: Local development and test runs should not require a database server, while production requires Supabase PostgreSQL; using a unified ORM layer allows URL-switchable backends.

nodes.label: ADR-011: xgboost-cpu in requirements
nodes.rationale: Default xgboost wheels pull large multi-hundred-MB CUDA libraries on Linux; using xgboost-cpu keeps installation and CI lightweight.
